title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu's Comeback Has a Saree, a Shotgun, and a Score to Settle
excerpt: Maa Inti Bangaaram arrives in theatres June 19 — a family action thriller she produced herself, with Santhosh Narayanan on the score and Gulshan Devaiah making his Telugu debut.
body:
The poster arrived in May and the internet hasn't recovered. Samantha Ruth Prabhu, draped in a deep crimson silk saree, bangles glinting at her wrists, fingers curled around a shotgun. The tagline: "Not everything has to glitter to be golden." If that doesn't tell you everything about Maa Inti Bangaaram, nothing will.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=B9d-wISnm8s

The film opens June 19, and it marks the kind of comeback that careers pivot around. Samantha hasn't graced the big screen in a while — not because she ran out of things to say, but because she was building the infrastructure to say it herself. Tralala Moving Pictures, her production house, isn't a vanity label. It's a declaration. And Maa Inti Bangaaram is its first major theatrical swing.

Directed by BV Nandini Reddy — who last teamed with Samantha on the hit Oh! Baby — the film was created and co-written by Raj Nidimoru, one half of the legendary Raj & DK duo and Samantha's husband. The story follows a woman who arrives at her in-laws' home as the new daughter-in-law: polite, composed, scrutinized for every breath she takes. The family doesn't trust her. What they don't know is what she's hiding.

"What I loved about Maa Inti Bangaaram is that it refuses to put women into boxes. It takes someone people may underestimate and turns her into the most powerful force in the room." — Samantha Ruth Prabhu

When the past she buried refuses to stay buried, the composure cracks — and the shotgun comes out. The trailer makes it clear: this isn't a demure family drama with one token fight scene. This is a full-blown action thriller wrapped inside a family story, with Samantha doing her own action sequences choreographed by Lee Whittaker and Aejaz Gulab. The double life is the USP — part homemaker scrutinized by suspicious in-laws, part lethal force hiding in plain sight.

Here's what makes the story behind the film as compelling as the one in it. Samantha revealed in a recent Instagram Q&A that Maa Inti Bangaaram wasn't originally hers. The role was first pitched to Sai Pallavi. "I didn't choose this movie, but this movie chose me," Samantha said. "The initial idea for this film was to pitch it to Sai Pallavi garu. I knew she was very busy and didn't have the time. Then the makers tweaked the film for me."

That kind of transparency is rare in an industry where casting decisions are typically buried under layers of PR. She tagged Sai Pallavi publicly and expressed hope to collaborate under Tralala in the future. That's a woman operating with nothing to prove and everything to gain.

The cast around her is quietly stacked. Gulshan Devaiah — the chameleon who's been electric in everything from Guns & Gulaabs to Dahaad, and fresh off the acclaim for Kantara: Chapter 1 — makes his Telugu debut here in what's described as a demanding, emotionally layered role. Diganth Manchale co-leads alongside Gautami Tadimalla, Sreemukhi, and Srinivas Gavireddy.

Then there's the music. Santhosh Narayanan — the man behind Karnan, Jai Bhim, and the thunderous Karuppu score — is composing here. The first single, "Thassadiyya," is already a certified earworm across Telugu-speaking audiences. With Om Prakash behind the camera and Raj Nidimoru shaping the screenplay, this is a seriously loaded creative team for what is technically an indie production.

For the diaspora, the timing is ideal. June 19 falls in a sweet spot between Cocktail 2's marketing blitz and the Welcome to the Jungle machine. Maa Inti Bangaaram releases worldwide, including across US, UK, and Canadian markets where Samantha's fanbase runs deep — built through Ye Maaya Chesave, Oh! Baby, and her scene-stealing turn in The Family Man Season 2. This is the kind of film NRI families will show up for: family drama meets action spectacle, led by a star who speaks directly to the South Indian diaspora.

The film was originally dated for May 15 but pushed to avoid the IPL frenzy — and to let Sunrisers Hyderabad fans focus on their season. With Peddi's theatrical dominance now cooling, the window for a mid-budget Telugu tentpole is wide open.

Samantha also has Rakt Brahmand: The Bloody Kingdom in the pipeline — a Raj & DK series co-starring Aditya Roy Kapur, Ali Fazal, and Wamiqa Gabbi — but Maa Inti Bangaaram is the one that counts right now. She is producing, starring, and leading from the front. If it lands, Tralala becomes one of Telugu cinema's most important new banners. If it doesn't, she'll still have walked back into the theater with a shotgun and a production credit.

Either way, she's not asking for permission.
